headline: High risk of capability conflict from ECC’s write-enabled workspace and git access; other pairwise risks are limited by python-cheatsheet’s documentation-only, no-IO profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write files, use MCP, and run browsers, so it could ingest content from shared files or copied outputs. python-cheatsheet has no clipboard, files, stdin/stdout, or MCP surfaces, so there is no direct automated bridge. The pathway is therefore limited to unusual manual transfer or an external shared workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a manually copied file or shared workspace, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF an external orchestrator feeds python-cheatsheet content into ECC as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or file-drop bridge.
Review copied content before pasting into ECC.
Use read-only exports for python-cheatsheet material.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to any shared content path.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, and local config files, but python-cheatsheet exposes no files, APIs, or stdout channel and handles no secrets. With no shared workspace or outbound channel on agent_b, leakage from ECC into python-cheatsheet is not a default pathway. The main risk is accidental local file exposure if an operator manually shares ECC artifacts.
conditions: IF the operator copies ECC session files into a shared directory, python-cheatsheet could expose them indirectly.
IF a future wrapper gives python-cheatsheet file access, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Do not place ECC artifacts in shared folders.
Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Redact session summaries before sharing.
Separate credentials from documentation files.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the launcher level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, git-state modification, shell, subprocess, and allowlisted network egress, while python-cheatsheet has no write, network, or process capabilities. The pair is asymmetric, but ECC alone can still mutate shared repos or files if co-located with other assets. Because ECC’s concurrency model warns about separate roots for multiple instances, uncertainty about shared-state collisions pushes this to high.
conditions: IF ECC and another writable workspace share the same root, file or git collisions can occur.
IF the operator places python-cheatsheet content inside a mutable repo, ECC may overwrite it.
mitigations: Use separate roots for each environment.
Mount python-cheatsheet content read-only.
Avoid running ECC in a repo with uncommitted work.
Commit or stash before launching ECC.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles around shared git/workspace state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and act on code, docs, and security findings, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream workflows. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot independently verify or execute actions, which limits blast radius. Still, if ECC-produced guidance is copied into python-cheatsheet-derived content, errors can cascade into user-facing documentation without verification.
conditions: IF ECC output is copied into documentation without review, incorrect guidance can propagate.
IF an external process treats ECC findings as final truth, downstream errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing ECC output.
Cross-check claims against source material.
Mark generated text as unverified.
Keep python-cheatsheet edits separate from ECC outputs.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream publication.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session summaries, skills, git history, and security findings, but the profile does not indicate regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII. python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no network or storage surfaces. With no documented residency or retention mismatch, compliance risk is limited to local handling hygiene rather than a concrete policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually inserted into ECC session files, compliance obligations may apply.
IF the operator stores ECC artifacts in a jurisdiction-restricted system, policy review is needed.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in session summaries.
Keep retention settings short.
Store artifacts in approved locations only.
Review access to git history before sharing.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for ECC outputs.
